decisionLog.outcome: Reset 2.2.2 under Andrew Wright, retiring the inherited delivery steps and resource assumptions and redrafting the proposition around partnership infrastructure, access funding, alumni and philanthropy. The proposition is now ready for informal stakeholder sense-check before formal Delivery design.

Rebased the recommended Core planning assumption for partnership infrastructure from £600,000 to £400,000 p.a. from 2027/28, while preserving Year 1 discovery and the requirement to produce lean, Core and more ambitious operating-model options from evidence. Student Opportunities Fund design remains within 2.2.2, but any new award pot is explicitly outside the King's Edge mobilisation ask and requires a separate institutional, consolidated-fund, philanthropic or other funding route.

decisionLog.forum: King's Edge Delivery Plan working update
decisionLog.outcome: Broaden 2.2.2 into Future-Proofed Employability & Experiential Infrastructure. Preserve the existing experiential partnership, access-funding, alumni and philanthropy work; add dedicated international employer-engagement and proactive graduate-transition capability; and retain a reduced £300,000 p.a. Core envelope for domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership infrastructure from 2027/28. Andrew Wright leads the deliverable with Eleanor Hannan as co-lead. The phased specified careers and employability resource ask is £390,354 annualised when fully mobilised: 1 x G6 and 3 x G5 international employer-engagement roles, a £50,000 international non-pay envelope, and 1 x G7 plus 1 x G6 Graduate Transitions roles. The first G6 and East Asia G5 are targeted for immediate mobilisation, Graduate Transitions from May 2027, and the remaining two international G5 roles from September 2027. Together with the £300,000 domestic experiential-infrastructure envelope, the fully mobilised annualised Core ask for 2.2.2 is £690,354, excluding any separately funded Student Opportunities Fund award pot.
